title: Treasury Laws Amendment (News Media and Digital Platforms Mandatory Bargaining Code) Bill 2021
description: Parliamentary record for the 2021 Mandatory Bargaining Code legislation, including passage dates and Act details.
supports: The Code was finally passed by both Houses on 25 February 2021 and received assent as Act No. 21 of 2021, commencing 2 March 2021.

title: News media bargaining code
description: ACCC overview of the Mandatory Bargaining Code framework and designation status.
supports: The Code addresses bargaining power imbalances between Australian news businesses and designated digital platforms. No digital platforms have yet been designated under the Code.

title: Treasury Laws Amendment (News Media and Digital Platforms Mandatory Bargaining Code) Act 2021
description: Authoritative text of the 2021 Act establishing the Mandatory Bargaining Code.
supports: Legal establishment of a mandatory code governing commercial relationships between Australian news businesses and designated digital platform corporations.

title: News Media Bargaining Charge Act 2026
description: Enacted legislation imposing the news media bargaining charge.
supports: The rate of charge is 2.75% (section 3). Assented to 26 August 2026; commenced with the Administration Act on 27 August 2026.

title: News Media Bargaining (Administration) Act 2026
description: Enacted administration framework for the News Media Incentive charge, offsets and eligibility.
supports: Sets the $250 million relevant Australian digital advertising revenue threshold; requires eligible expenditure with at least 8 different news business corporate groups for offset entitlement; and limits any one group's adjusted contribution to one quarter (25%) of the NMI amount.

title: News Media Bargaining (Administration) Bill 2026 [and related Bills] — Bills Digest
description: Parliamentary Library bills digest explaining the NMI framework, offset calculation and policy rationale.
supports: Explains the 8-group minimum as designed to encourage sustainability and diversity by preventing offset through only a small number of groups, and documents the 25% single-group cap in offset calculation.

title: News Media Bargaining Charge Bill 2026 — Explanatory Memorandum (Parliamentary Amendments)
description: Explanatory memorandum for parliamentary amendments increasing the NMI rate.
supports: Documents the move from a 2.5% design rate to an enacted 2.75% rate, reflecting market changes since 2021 deals.

title: News Media Bargaining (Administration) Bill 2026 [and related Bills] — Bills Digest (revenue estimates)
description: Ministerial estimates quoted in the bills digest regarding expected media benefit under deals versus charge pathways.
supports: Records government estimates of roughly $200–250 million via commercial dealings, or roughly $350–400 million per year if platforms pay the charge — and that charge receipts are directed to the News Journalism Payment Scheme.

title: Final legislation — News media bargaining code
description: ACCC page linking to final 2021 legislation as passed.
supports: Confirms final passage of the Mandatory Bargaining Code legislation on 25 February 2021.
